title: Limits and warnings
summary: What happens as a billing account nears and passes an allowance. The middle row is the same for every counted kind: resolve the allowance, then warn the owners once at 80% and once when it is used up. Above it is what never stops, below it what is refused. Each check lives where the count changes, in Laravel; the runtime enforces nothing.

boxes.label: A count changes
boxes.detail: There is no central gate. Usage::add counts data points (from DataPointReports) and alerts (from AlertProjector), Usage::reserve counts SMS parts, and DeviceLimit::claim gives a device a place when its activation is accepted. Each runs under a row lock, so concurrent counts for one account serialize.

boxes.label: Allowances::resolve
boxes.detail: The account's allowance for a kind is its override, else its open plan's value, else the deployment default in config/billing.php. Null is unlimited, except retention, where it means the platform's setting. An account with no plan gets the defaults: unlimited alerts, devices and data points, and one organization.

boxes.label: UsageThresholds
boxes.detail: Called once the counting transaction commits, for alerts, SMS, data points and devices. A threshold is passed when count x 100 >= percent x allowance. An unlimited allowance sends nothing, and neither does a count of 0, even against an allowance of 0. A count that jumps past both sends both.

boxes.label: Notices ledger
boxes.detail: Inserts a billing_notices row keyed {kind}:{YYYY-MM}:{80|100} and queues the emails in the same transaction only when the row was new, so a warning is never sent twice. An account with no owners gets no notice. billing:prune removes rows after 13 months.

boxes.label: Account owners
boxes.detail: DeliverBillingEmail sends one email per owner on the alerts database queue, five tries with backoff of 1, 5 and 15 minutes. It skips anyone who is no longer an owner or has no verified address by then. The email names the allowance, what is used and left, and links to the portal's Billing accounts page.

boxes.label: Overage
boxes.detail: Past the allowance an alert still fires and a reading is still stored. The part beyond the allowance at that moment is added to billing_usage.overage and to billing_overage under the plan assignment in force, where the invoice prices it: alerts one by one, data points by whole blocks, nothing for a day that began on a trial. A later allowance change moves only what is left.

boxes.label: SMS not reserved
boxes.detail: SMS parts are reserved before sending, not counted after: when they do not fit in what is left, reserve answers false, counts nothing and sends the 100% warning. SMS never has overage, and release gives parts back when the provider refuses a message. This is the SmsAllowance contract; no SMS sender in the code calls it yet.

boxes.label: Organization refused
boxes.detail: An owner creating an organization under the account is refused with a validation error once the account has as many organizations as its organizations allowance, checked under the account's row lock. The check is in the owner's path only; a platform administrator creating one is not bound by it. No warning is sent for this kind.

boxes.label: Retention confirmation
boxes.detail: Retention is a setting, not a count. A plan change, plan edit, override or organization move that would shorten an organization's telemetry retention answers 409 until it is repeated with confirm_retention. Once confirmed, cleanup keeps the previous period for BILLING_RETENTION_GRACE_DAYS (30) and the owners are emailed.

boxes.label: Activation refused
boxes.detail: DeviceLimit::claim locks the billing account's row, counts the places held across its organizations and throws DeviceLimitReached when the count has reached the limit. A device that already holds a place keeps it, so reconfiguring or rolling back is never refused, and a move inside the account hands the place over without a check. Bulk onboarding leaves each source beyond the limit registered, with the reason.

boxes.label: Over the limit
boxes.detail: Lowering the device limit, or moving an organization into the account, can leave more devices holding a place than the limit allows. Nothing is deactivated: DeviceLimit::recheck raises the month's peak and checks the warnings, usage shows over_limit, and activations are refused until the count is back below the limit.

steps.text: Whatever changes a count asks for the account's allowance of that kind: its override, else its plan's value, else the deployment default.
After the count commits, a limited allowance is checked at 80% and at 100%. Unlimited allowances are counted and never warned about.
A passed threshold tries to insert its notice, keyed by kind, month and threshold.
Only a new key queues the emails, one per owner, so each warning goes out once per month.
Past the allowance, alerts keep firing and readings keep being stored. What went past is recorded as overage for the invoice.
An SMS that no longer fits is not reserved, so the sender must not send it. SMS has no overage.
A device activation at the limit is refused with a 422. Devices that already hold a place are never touched.
A lowered limit deactivates nothing: the account reads over the limit and further activations are refused until it is back below.
An owner at the organization limit cannot create another organization under the account.
A change that would shorten retention needs confirmation, and then history is kept for a 30-day grace before cleanup shortens it.
